title: Rule from Damascus
hookLine: Mu'awiyah rules from Damascus, and the caliphate becomes a dynasty

cards: Medina had been the center. The Prophet, peace be upon him, was buried there. Abu Bakr, Umar and Uthman had led from there.

Ali had moved to Kufa, in Iraq. And now the seat of the Muslim community moves again, north, to an old city: Damascus. The man ruling from there is Mu'awiyah, who had governed Syria under the earlier caliphs.
With him, the question that had split the believers since the day after the Prophet's death takes a new shape. Not only who should lead, but how leadership passes on.

teach.b: Each caliph so far had come to office a different way. Abu Bakr by a pledge in a meeting hall. Umar named by Abu Bakr.
Uthman chosen by a council. Ali by a pledge in the mosque, in a crisis. None was a son taking over from a father.

teach.h: A PLEDGE FOR YAZID, IN ADVANCE.
teach.b: The histories report that in his later years Mu'awiyah asked the people to pledge loyalty, in advance, to his son Yazid.
Some refused; several sons of the great companions in Medina are reported among them, and so is Husayn. But the pledge was taken, and when Mu'awiyah died, Yazid ruled.
The rule of one family, the Umayyads, had begun, passing from father to son, or cousin to cousin, for generations.

A hadith in Abu Dawud and Tirmidhi says that the caliphate of prophethood would last thirty years, and after it God would give kingship to whom He wills. In Arabic, the word for that kingship is mulk.
Some scholars read that hadith against this very moment.

teach.h: SUNNI AND SHIA SEE HIM DIFFERENTLY.
teach.b: Sunni and Shia Muslims see Mu'awiyah differently.

Sunni Muslims count him a companion of the Prophet, and Sunni teaching gives him the respect owed to companions, while some Sunni scholars are frank that turning the caliphate into an inheritance was a change for the worse.
Shia Muslims see him as the man who fought Ali, the rightful Imam, and who set the stage for the tragedy that came next. Either way, a community that had chosen its leaders now inherited them.

how: Muslims remember the move of the caliphate to Damascus under Mu'awiyah as the start of the Umayyad dynasty; Sunni Muslims honor him as a companion while often criticizing the hereditary turn, and Shia Muslims remember him as Ali's opponent.

games.q: you're Mu'awiyah, old and ruling from Damascus. you have to decide what happens after you. what do you do?
o: leave it to a council, as with Uthman.
ask the people to pledge to your son now.
name no one and let the people choose.
games.why: the histories report he asked for a pledge to Yazid in advance, and some in Medina refused.

practice: Bring to mind something handed down to you that you didn't choose: a family business, a role, a name, a way of doing things, even a grudge.
Ask which parts came to you because they were right, and which only because they were yours. Then think of one thing you will hand on, and how it could pass fairly.

wordCard.voice: Mulk, kingship: the hadith's word for the rule God gives after the caliphate of prophethood, the moment Mu'awiyah's rule began to pass from father to son. Today's word.

orig.note: Arabic: kingship or dominion, the word in the hadith for rule that comes after the caliphate of prophethood.

carryVoice: Your line: a dynasty begins. It would run for generations. Day eight hundred eighty-eight, done.
